criteria.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry (for example id "behavior-evidence") with applies_to ["*"], a source citing this request, and a statement whose FIRST sentence states the core rule (criteria check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist), because the rendered brief shows only the first sentence.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: defaults.toml adds id "behavior-evidence" with applies_to = ["*"] and source "Job 20261015-095214-y8kr user request ...". Its first sentence is "Every acceptance criterion checks the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist."

criteria.criterion: The statement's later sentences require that any protection/denial test first shows the action succeeds without the protection, under the same user and environment the real component runs as (root), then shows it is refused, and that if the environment cannot enforce the protection the test fails rather than skips or passes silently.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: the second sentence says the test "first shows the action succeeds without the protection, as the same user and in the same environment the real component runs as (root here), and then shows it is refused". The third says "If the environment cannot enforce the protection, the test fails; it does not skip or pass silently" and that a check root bypasses is not proof.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the repository defaults.toml and asserts the new entry exists and its render() line appears with the core rule; run `cargo test -p athena-data` and see it pass, while existing tests (including root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule) still pass.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 64 passed, 0 failed, including behavior_evidence_default_leads_with_the_core_rule and root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule. The new test parses REPO_DEFAULTS, checks applies_to, checks the exact rendered line, and checks that the later sentences are in the statement but not in the rendered output. It would fail without the entry, because model.get(...).unwrap() would panic.

criteria.criterion: A worked example (docs/design/defaults-loop.md or a doc test fixture) shows a reading for 'make X read-only' whose criteria are: (1) a write to X as root succeeds before protection, (2) after protection the same write as root is refused, (3) the test fails, not skips, if the environment cannot enforce it (e.g. a root-bypassed file mode is not accepted as proof).
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: §3.7 of defaults-loop.md has three criteria that match (1)–(3) exactly, including "A file mode alone is not accepted as proof, because root bypasses it". It also lists rejected forms.

criteria.criterion: A second worked example for 'role calls a model' has criteria that run the role end to end and check the model call is made and its output is used (for example through the fake client, with the request observed), not merely that a client type or config is wired in.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: §3.7's 'the reviewer role calls a model' example runs the role end to end against the fake client, observes the request the fake received, and checks that the result contains the fake's reply, and that changing the reply changes the result. It rejects wiring-only forms.

findings.evidence: Line 13 now reads "...existence alone does not suffice.- deliverables: every path you expect to change..." with no newline. This change introduced it; in the base, the two were separate bullets. The reader frame is sent to every reader, and its deliverables rule (unlisted paths cost about 1) is now hidden inside the acceptance_criteria bullet.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG entry says something untrue: 'the reader prompt names the protection rule'.
findings.evidence: The reader.md diff only shortens existing wording (title/summary, producer_model, acceptance_criteria, deliverables bullets). It adds nothing about protection or denial tests; a Grep of crates/athena-context for 'protection' finds no match in reader.md.

findings.summary: The reader prompt's wording was trimmed without the request asking for it, and the change does not explain why.
findings.evidence: Several guidance lines were shortened, for example 'before assuming' was removed and 'criteria that only test that something exists' became 'existence alone does not suffice'. The likely reason (an inference, not confirmed) is that the reader set's 1,930-token budget in athena-context/src/lib.rs had to make room for the new rendered default. If so, the CHANGELOG should say so. Out-of-scope lists changing how prompts are built beyond the defaults rendering.

summary: I failed this change: it does what the request asked, but it has two major defects elsewhere. The new `behavior-evidence` default is correct. It applies to all work, starts with the core rule (every acceptance criterion checks the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist), then gives the rules for testing a protection: first succeed as root without it, then be refused, and fail rather than skip. A new unit test checks the entry and the line the reader sees, and the design doc has good worked examples for 'make X read-only' and 'role calls a model'. `cargo test -p athena-data`, fmt and clippy pass in my runs. My full `cargo test` run finished without a reported error, but policy kept me from reading its totals; Athena's own run passed 685 tests. The defects: (1) the edit to the reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md) joined the acceptance_criteria and deliverables bullets into one line, so the reader now gets a malformed deliverables rule; (2) the CHANGELOG says the reader prompt now names the protection rule, but it doesn't. The reader prompt was only shortened, probably to stay within its token budget, though the change doesn't say so. To fix: restore the line break and correct or remove the CHANGELOG claim.
